purpose: Choose no stale cutoff or recency weighting until forecast accuracy is tested prospectively/out-of-sample; preserve forecast age as data rather than hard-coding freshness.
population: Taiwan listed/OTC symbols only when an authorized PIT analyst-estimate source satisfies ANALYST_FORECAST_REVISION_PIT_CONTRACT; otherwise UNKNOWN and no empirical join.
unitOfObservation: individual analyst/broker forecast vintage x symbol x target fiscal horizon x decision timestamp
primaryDiagnostics: absolute EPS forecast error by age bucket
signed EPS forecast error by age bucket
consensus absolute error under equal-weight latest-active-per-forecaster
coverage and dispersion by age bucket
weightingRule: Do not optimize decay half-life. If recency weighting is tested, use one predeclared simple monotone scheme and compare against equal-weight baseline.
antiLeakage: forecast must be published/observed before decisionAt
actual EPS enters only after its first-known release and only as evaluation target
horizon roll is not a revision
withdrawn forecasts remain in lineage but are inactive for later consensus
missing forecast age or timestamp => UNKNOWN
falsification: If forecast age has no stable monotone relation with OOS accuracy, reject stale cutoff/recency weighting.
If gains are driven by one sector, one coverage regime, one forecaster or announcement-adjacent revisions, mark fragile.
If recency weighting improves in-sample but not purged/OOS/prospective results, retain equal-weight baseline.
If source population changes over time or correction lineage is unproven, do not attribute differences to forecast freshness.
literatureContext: Prior research reports informed consensus weights using forecast age plus analyst/broker attributes can improve forecast accuracy versus naive consensus; this motivates a challenger, not an imported Taiwan threshold.
